feature: Title and Gfx tracks wear the title mock's icons
summary: A track holding a title now shows the text mark in its header, and a track holding a logo or picture laid over the video shows the sparkle, as the title mock draws them beside V1. Before, both wore the same stacked-layers icon.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording with the timeline open; import a PNG with File > Import Media.

try.do: Move the playhead to two seconds.
Drag the logo's tile from the Library's Media shelf over V1 at two seconds and let go.
Open Comps in the Library and double-click Keynote Clean.
Click the empty canvas so nothing is picked, and look at the track headers.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Read the column of headers: Title, Gfx, V1.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Can you tell the title track from the logo track by its icon alone, before reading its name?
Does the sparkle read as 'graphic' to you, or would a picture icon say it better?
The title clip is now the dark text colour the mock gives titles, no longer teal: does that read better on the timeline?
rough: A title's clip changed colour with its icon: it was overlay teal and is now the dark text clip, so it matches the mock (video-title-wt.html .clip.txt).
The logo's clip is still overlay teal where video-title-wt.html draws Gfx clips amber (a-logo-or-picture-clip-on-a-gfx-track-wears-the).
A screenshot with no time of its own (the picture a motion document is drawn over) keeps the stacked-layers icon; only a picture placed for a stretch of the video counts as Gfx.
Shapes and arrows drawn over a video still wear the stacked-layers icon; no mock gives them a track of their own.
Pictures were taken with the window behind another app, so picked controls show their background colour.
